title: Ruth 2: Gleaning in the Field of Boaz
body:
Read the chapter → [Ruth 2](/bible/ruth/2)

**[Ruth 2:1-3](/bible/ruth/2#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/ruth/2#v1)</sup> And Naomi had a kinsman of her husband’s, a mighty man of wealth, of the family of Elimelech; and his name was Boaz.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/ruth/2#v2)</sup> And Ruth the Moabitess said unto Naomi, Let me now go to the field, and glean ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace. And she said unto her, Go, my daughter.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/ruth/2#v3)</sup> And she went, and came, and gleaned in the field after the reapers: and her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging unto Boaz, who was of the kindred of Elimelech.

- Naomi had a kinsman of her husband, a mighty man of wealth of the family of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz.
- Ruth asked Naomi, Let me now go to the field and glean ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace; and her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging unto Boaz, who was of the kindred of Elimelech.

**[Ruth 2:4-9](/bible/ruth/2#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/ruth/2#v4)</sup> And, behold, Boaz came from Beth–lehem, and said unto the reapers, The Lord be with you. And they answered him, The Lord bless thee.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/ruth/2#v5)</sup> Then said Boaz unto his servant that was set over the reapers, Whose damsel is this?
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/ruth/2#v6)</sup> And the servant that was set over the reapers answered and said, It is the Moabitish damsel that came back with Naomi out of the country of Moab:
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/ruth/2#v7)</sup> And she said, I pray you, let me glean and gather after the reapers among the sheaves: so she came, and hath continued even from the morning until now, that she tarried a little in the house.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/ruth/2#v8)</sup> Then said Boaz unto Ruth, Hearest thou not, my daughter? Go not to glean in another field, neither go from hence, but abide here fast by my maidens:
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/ruth/2#v9)</sup> Let thine eyes be on the field that they do reap, and go thou after them: have I not charged the young men that they shall not touch thee? and when thou art athirst, go unto the vessels, and drink of that which the young men have drawn.

- Boaz came from Bethlehem and greeted his reapers, The Lord be with you; and they answered him, The Lord bless thee. When he asked whose damsel this was, the servant set over the reapers answered, It is the Moabitish damsel that came back with Naomi, and reported how she had asked to glean and had continued from the morning with only a little rest in the house.
- Boaz told Ruth to glean in no other field but to abide fast by his maidens; he had charged the young men not to touch her, and when she was athirst she could drink of the vessels the young men had drawn.

**[Ruth 2:10](/bible/ruth/2#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/ruth/2#v10)</sup> Then she fell on her face, and bowed herself to the ground, and said unto him, Why have I found grace in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger?

- Ruth fell on her face and asked, Why have I found grace in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger? She acknowledged what she was to Israel: a stranger.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Esdras 8:69](/bible/1-esdras/8#v69)**
    > <sup>[69](/bible/1-esdras/8#v69)</sup> The nation of Israel, the princes, the priests and Levites, have not put away from them the strange people of the land, nor the pollutions of the Gentiles to wit, of the Canaanites, Hittites, Pheresites, Jebusites, and the Moabites, Egyptians, and Edomites.

    The Moabites are counted among the strange people of the land; Ruth spoke of herself by that same word.
  - **[Leviticus 25:44-46](/bible/leviticus/25#v44)**
    > <sup>[44](/bible/leviticus/25#v44)</sup> Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids.
    >
    > <sup>[45](/bible/leviticus/25#v45)</sup> Moreover of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that are with you, which they begat in your land: and they shall be your possession.
    >
    > <sup>[46](/bible/leviticus/25#v46)</sup> And ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them for a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever: but over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.

    The bondmen and bondmaids of Israel shall be of the heathen round about and of the children of the strangers that sojourn among you; they shall be your possession. When we get into the kingdom this order will be in place.

**[Ruth 2:11-13](/bible/ruth/2#v11)**

> <sup>[11](/bible/ruth/2#v11)</sup> And Boaz answered and said unto her, It hath fully been shewed me, all that thou hast done unto thy mother in law since the death of thine husband: and how thou hast left thy father and thy mother, and the land of thy nativity, and art come unto a people which thou knewest not heretofore.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/ruth/2#v12)</sup> The Lord recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the Lord God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/ruth/2#v13)</sup> Then she said, Let me find favour in thy sight, my lord; for that thou hast comforted me, and for that thou hast spoken friendly unto thine handmaid, though I be not like unto one of thine handmaidens.

- Boaz answered that it had fully been shewed him all she had done for her mother in law since the death of her husband, how she left her father, her mother, and the land of her nativity, and came unto a people she knew not before.
- The Lord recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the Lord God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust. Ruth answered, Let me find favour in thy sight, my lord, for thou hast comforted me, though I be not like unto one of thine handmaidens.

**[Ruth 2:14-17](/bible/ruth/2#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/ruth/2#v14)</sup> And Boaz said unto her, At mealtime come thou hither, and eat of the bread, and dip thy morsel in the vinegar. And she sat beside the reapers: and he reached her parched corn, and she did eat, and was sufficed, and left.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/ruth/2#v15)</sup> And when she was risen up to glean, Boaz commanded his young men, saying, Let her glean even among the sheaves, and reproach her not:
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/ruth/2#v16)</sup> And let fall also some of the handfuls of purpose for her, and leave them, that she may glean them, and rebuke her not.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/ruth/2#v17)</sup> So she gleaned in the field until even, and beat out that she had gleaned: and it was about an ephah of barley.

- At mealtime Boaz told her to come and eat of the bread and dip her morsel in the vinegar; he reached her parched corn, and she did eat and was sufficed and left.
- When she rose to glean, Boaz commanded his young men to let her glean even among the sheaves without reproach, and to let fall handfuls of purpose for her. She gleaned until evening and beat out about an ephah of barley.

**[Ruth 2:18-23](/bible/ruth/2#v18)**

> <sup>[18](/bible/ruth/2#v18)</sup> And she took it up, and went into the city: and her mother in law saw what she had gleaned: and she brought forth, and gave to her that she had reserved after she was sufficed.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/ruth/2#v19)</sup> And her mother in law said unto her, Where hast thou gleaned to day? and where wroughtest thou? blessed be he that did take knowledge of thee. And she shewed her mother in law with whom she had wrought, and said, The man’s name with whom I wrought to day is Boaz.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/ruth/2#v20)</sup> And Naomi said unto her daughter in law, Blessed be he of the Lord, who hath not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead. And Naomi said unto her, The man is near of kin unto us, one of our next kinsmen.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/ruth/2#v21)</sup> And Ruth the Moabitess said, He said unto me also, Thou shalt keep fast by my young men, until they have ended all my harvest.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/ruth/2#v22)</sup> And Naomi said unto Ruth her daughter in law, It is good, my daughter, that thou go out with his maidens, that they meet thee not in any other field.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/ruth/2#v23)</sup> So she kept fast by the maidens of Boaz to glean unto the end of barley harvest and of wheat harvest; and dwelt with her mother in law.

- Ruth brought what she had gleaned into the city, gave Naomi what she had reserved, and told her, The man's name with whom I wrought to day is Boaz.
- Naomi blessed him of the Lord, who hath not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead, and said, The man is near of kin unto us, one of our next kinsmen.
- Naomi told her it was good to go out with his maidens, that they meet thee not in any other field; so Ruth kept fast by the maidens of Boaz to glean unto the end of barley harvest and of wheat harvest, and dwelt with her mother in law.
